entries.title: Basic Anatomy Review (Forearm/Hand Musculature, Tendon Compartments, Facial Skeleton)

testable_competencies.anatomy: Foundational forearm/hand tendon-compartment and facial-skeleton anatomy that frames later chapter content but is not independently tested.

entries.zero_question_reason: Specialist-technique, cosmetic/elective-procedure, or foundational-background content with no independently testable generalist competency identified; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage.

entries.title: Skin Lesions and Masses: Differential Diagnosis and Surgical Management of Malignant Lesions

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 38's scope ('diagnose the cause, severity and complications' of a skin condition, with particular attention to whether a lesion is benign, malignant, or systemic) directly covers recognizing a suspicious skin lesion/mass and determining that it requires excision, which is this unit's core generalist-relevant content.

testable_competencies.recognition: Generate a differential diagnosis for a skin lesion/mass and recognize features suggesting malignancy requiring surgical referral/excision.
testable_competencies.management: Understand that surgical excision is the primary management for malignant skin lesions and that margins are determined by lesion depth/type.

do_not_test: Exact numeric excision-margin tables by melanoma Breslow depth (specialist-level technical detail; overlaps Dermatology's staging-driven management).
entries.cross_discipline_note: Diagnostic/pathophysiology content for these lesions is primarily owned by Dermatology (explicit in-text redirect to D4/D8/D40); this unit retains only the surgical-management/referral angle. PRIMARY_OWNER vs. CROSS_LINK deferred to global cross-chapter audit per project instruction.

entries.title: Suturing and Wound Closure Materials

testable_competencies.technique: General awareness that suture material choice (absorbable vs. non-absorbable) depends on wound location, tension, and healing time.

entries.zero_question_reason: Suture-material selection detail and knot/technique are procedural skills assessed in clinical training rather than MCCQE1-style single-best-answer items; no dedicated MCC objective anchors this content independently of the broader Skin wounds objective (109-12), which is represented on the Wound Classification and Assessment unit instead.

entries.title: Skin Biopsy Types and Excisional Techniques

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Selecting an appropriate biopsy technique (shave, punch, incisional, excisional) for a suspicious skin lesion is part of objective 38's diagnostic-workup scope ('diagnose the cause... whether a condition is benign, malignant or associated with an underlying systemic condition').

testable_competencies.technique_selection: Select the appropriate biopsy technique (shave vs. punch vs. incisional vs. excisional) based on lesion characteristics and suspected diagnosis.

do_not_test: Step-by-step operative excision technique (specialist procedural skill).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 109-12's key/enabling objectives explicitly require diagnosing wound cause/severity/complications, assessing for underlying tendon/nerve/vessel injury and contamination before closure, and considering tetanus status -- this unit's core content (wound type/mechanism classification and pre-closure assessment) is a direct match.

testable_competencies.assessment: Classify wound type (laceration, puncture, crush, avulsion, abrasion) and assess for underlying tendon/nerve/vascular injury, contamination, and tetanus-immunization status prior to closure.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Recognizing and managing wound infection is part of objective 109-12's 'complications' scope for skin wounds.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Also falls within objective 38's general skin-condition complication scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize clinical signs of wound infection and initiate appropriate management (debridement, antibiotics, delayed closure).

entries.title: Wound Dressings

testable_competencies.principles: General awareness that dressing choice (moist wound healing, negative-pressure wound therapy) depends on wound characteristics.

entries.zero_question_reason: Specialist-technique, cosmetic/elective-procedure, or foundational-background content with no independently testable generalist competency identified; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage.

testable_competencies.concept: Recognize the reconstructive-ladder concept (primary closure -> healing by secondary intention -> skin graft -> local/regional flap -> free flap) as a framework for escalating wound-closure complexity, without needing to select or perform a specific technique.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 38 directly covers diagnosing a skin/integument condition's cause, severity, and complications -- erysipelas/cellulitis are canonical presentations of this objective.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Differentiate erysipelas from cellulitis by depth/margin characteristics and identify risk factors (PVD, DM, lymphedema, portal of entry).
testable_competencies.management: Initiate appropriate empiric antibiotic therapy and recognize when IV therapy or admission is warranted.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: A life-threatening skin/soft-tissue condition squarely within objective 38's severity/complication-recognition scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize red-flag features of necrotizing fasciitis (pain out of proportion, rapidly spreading erythema, crepitus, systemic toxicity) and initiate emergent surgical consultation.

entries.title: Lower Limb (Venous, Arterial, and Diabetic) Ulcers

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Chronic lower-limb ulcer differentiation and management is within objective 38's cause/severity/complications scope for skin conditions.

testable_competencies.differential: Differentiate venous, arterial, and diabetic/neuropathic ulcers by location, appearance, and associated findings; recognize need for vascular workup.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Substantial overlap with Vascular Surgery (arterial ulcer workup/revascularization) and General/Thoracic Surgery/Endocrinology (diabetic foot). PRIMARY_OWNER/CROSS_LINK deferred to global cross-chapter audit.

entries.title: Pressure Ulcers (Pressure Injuries)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Pressure-injury staging/prevention/management is within objective 38's skin-condition severity/management scope.

testable_competencies.staging: Stage a pressure injury and recognize prevention strategies (repositioning, offloading, skin care) and indications for surgical debridement/referral.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Substantial overlap with Geriatric Medicine and Palliative Medicine (immobile/end-of-life patients). PRIMARY_OWNER/CROSS_LINK deferred to global cross-chapter audit.

entries.title: Burn Injury Classification, Pathophysiology, and Severity Assessment

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: No MCC objective is dedicated to burns specifically (full-registry search for 'burn' returned zero matches); objective 109's general trauma scope -- diagnose cause, severity, and complications of an injury -- covers conceptual burn-depth/extent recognition as a trauma subtype.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Burn wounds are also a skin/integument condition within objective 38's general scope, though the registry has no burn-specific enabling objective.

testable_competencies.classification: Classify burn depth (superficial, partial-thickness, full-thickness) by clinical appearance and estimate extent conceptually (rule of nines / palmar surface).
testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize the zone-of-injury model (hyperemia, stasis, coagulation) as it relates to burn progression and resuscitation urgency.

do_not_test: Exact histologic zone boundaries or burn-depth grading criteria beyond the conceptual superficial/partial/full-thickness distinction.

entries.title: Indications for Referral to a Burn Centre

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Recognizing severe/complicated trauma requiring specialized-centre referral is part of objective 109's general management-plan scope.

testable_competencies.triage: Recognize burn characteristics (TBSA threshold, depth, special-site involvement, inhalation injury, patient factors) that mandate transfer to a specialized burn centre.

entries.title: Acute Care and Initial Resuscitation of Burn Patients

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Initiating an appropriate management plan (ABCs, fluid resuscitation, wound care) for a severe trauma patient is objective 109's core scope.

testable_competencies.stabilization: Apply primary-survey (ABCs) principles to a major burn patient, recognize airway-compromise risk from inhalation injury, and understand that fluid resuscitation is guided by TBSA and weight-based formulas.

do_not_test: Exact current fluid-resuscitation formula and rate (e.g., Parkland-type calculations) -- per project instruction, changing numeric protocols are not frozen at scope stage and will be verified against current guidelines during question generation.

entries.title: Special Considerations in Burn Injury (Chemical, Electrical, Inhalation, Pediatric)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Special burn mechanisms (chemical, electrical, inhalation) remain within objective 109's general trauma-complications scope, though no dedicated objective addresses them individually.

testable_competencies.special_mechanisms: Recognize distinguishing features and additional risks of chemical, electrical, and inhalation burns, and features prompting suspicion of non-accidental (pediatric) burn injury.

entries.title: Approach to and General Management of Traumatic Hand Injuries

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 109-11 requires confirming the diagnosis, cause, severity, and complications of a nerve injury and identifying the peripheral nerves/level involved -- directly matches this unit's nerve-examination content.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 109-15 (Vascular injury) covers the vascular-assessment component of the general hand-injury exam.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 109-3 (Bone or joint injury) covers the skeletal-assessment component.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 109-12 (Skin wounds) explicitly requires assessing for underlying tendon/nerve/vessel injury before wound closure -- the core generalist skill this unit teaches.

testable_competencies.examination: Perform and interpret a systematic hand exam (skin, tendon, nerve, vessel, bone) after trauma, including testing nerve function before local anesthesia.
testable_competencies.triage: Distinguish injuries requiring emergent OR exploration from those suitable for delayed/outpatient management.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Hand infections (paronychia, felon, flexor tenosynovitis, deep-space infections) are skin/soft-tissue conditions within objective 38's diagnosis/severity/complications scope.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Overlaps objective 109-12's wound-infection complication scope when infection follows a traumatic wound.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize the clinical features of common hand infections (paronychia, felon, flexor tenosynovitis/Kanavel signs, deep-space infection) and identify which require urgent surgical drainage.

entries.title: Traumatic Hand Amputations and Replantation

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Vascular assessment/preservation of an amputated part is within objective 109-15's revascularization-urgency scope.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Overlaps 109-3's bone/joint injury scope for the skeletal component of amputation injuries.

testable_competencies.initial_management: Recognize appropriate initial management and transport of an amputated digit/part (wrap in saline gauze, place in bag on ice, avoid direct ice contact) and identify replantation candidacy factors requiring urgent referral.

do_not_test: Microsurgical replantation technique itself (specialist operative skill).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 109-12's enabling objectives explicitly list 'signs and symptoms suggestive of underlying injury to tendon, nerve or blood vessel' as a required assessment before wound closure -- tendon injury recognition is directly named.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize clinical signs of flexor vs. extensor tendon injury (loss of active flexion/extension at the relevant joint) and understand the greater urgency of flexor tendon repair due to retraction risk.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 109-3 (Bone or joint injury) directly covers diagnosing hand/finger fracture and dislocation cause, severity, and complications.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize common hand fracture patterns (boxer's fracture, Bennett/Rolando, mallet finger) and joint dislocations, and identify which require urgent reduction or surgical referral.
Recognize palmar fascia thickening/cords and progressive digit contracture as features of Dupuytren's disease, and that surgical release is indicated once contracture limits function.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 66 (Numbness/tingling/altered sensation) covers the presenting-symptom diagnostic workup that carpal tunnel syndrome is a classic cause of; no dedicated 'compressive neuropathy' or 'carpal tunnel' MCC objective exists (confirmed via full-registry search).

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize median-nerve distribution numbness/tingling and provocative-test findings (Tinel's, Phalen's) suggesting carpal tunnel syndrome, and identify conservative vs. surgical management indications.

entries.title: Brachial Plexus Injuries

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 109-11 (Nerve injury) covers diagnosing cause/severity/complications and identifying the level/type of nerve involvement -- directly applicable to brachial plexus trauma, though no dedicated brachial-plexus objective exists.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize the clinical presentation of traction/compressive vs. sharp/open brachial plexus injury (including obstetric palsy) and distinguish findings suggesting root avulsion.
testable_competencies.referral: Identify indications for urgent surgical exploration (open/sharp injury) vs. observation (closed traction injury).

do_not_test: Nerve transfer/grafting surgical technique selection (specialist reconstructive skill).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 109-8's key objective is exactly this content: 'given a patient with a facial injury, the candidate will diagnose the cause, severity, and complications and initiate an appropriate management plan. In particular, the candidate will assess and control vital functions and give management priority to life-threatening injuries.'

testable_competencies.primary_survey: Apply ABCs/primary-survey principles to a facial trauma patient, prioritizing airway control and identifying life-threatening associated injuries before detailed facial assessment.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: A named facial-injury subtype within objective 109-8's scope; no dedicated mandible-fracture MCC objective exists (confirmed via full-registry search).

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize clinical features suggesting mandible fracture (malocclusion, trismus, step deformity, numb chin) and the need for imaging and maxillofacial/plastic surgery referral.

entries.title: Maxillary (Le Fort) Fractures

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: A named facial-injury subtype within objective 109-8's scope; no dedicated Le Fort/maxillary-fracture MCC objective exists.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize features of midface instability (Le Fort pattern) and the airway/CSF-leak risks that mandate urgent evaluation.

do_not_test: Detailed Le Fort I/II/III surgical fixation planning (specialist operative detail).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: A named facial-injury subtype within objective 109-8's scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize nasal fracture and, critically, identify septal hematoma requiring urgent drainage to prevent cartilage necrosis/saddle-nose deformity.

entries.title: Zygomatic Fractures

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: A named facial-injury subtype within objective 109-8's scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize the pathognomonic triad (subconjunctival hemorrhage, periorbital ecchymosis, infraorbital/CN V2 numbness) and malar flattening suggesting zygomatic complex fracture.

do_not_test: Gillies vs. Keen approach selection for disimpaction (specialist operative technique).

entries.title: Orbital Floor Fractures

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: A named facial-injury subtype within objective 109-8's scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize blow-out orbital floor fracture presentation (enophthalmos, diplopia on upgaze from inferior rectus entrapment, infraorbital numbness) and urgent ophthalmology co-management indications.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Explicit in-text cross-reference to Ophthalmology (OP42); PRIMARY_OWNER/CROSS_LINK deferred to global cross-chapter audit.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: A named facial/ear-injury subtype within objective 109-8's scope; overlaps Otolaryngology.

testable_competencies.management: Recognize auricular hematoma after blunt ear trauma and the need for prompt (within 72h, up to 7d) aspiration/incision-and-drainage plus splinting to prevent avascular necrosis and cauliflower-ear deformity.

entries.title: Breast Anatomy (Vascular Supply and Innervation)

testable_competencies.anatomy: Foundational breast vascular supply and dermatomal innervation that frames the breast-surgery units below.

entries.zero_question_reason: Specialist-technique, cosmetic/elective-procedure, or foundational-background content with no independently testable generalist competency identified; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage.

entries.title: Breast Reduction (Reduction Mammaplasty)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 10-1's scope (breast mass/enlargement diagnosis and management) touches the symptomatic-macromastia indication for reduction, though the objective is framed around diagnosing a presenting mass/enlargement rather than elective symptomatic reduction, and no dedicated MCCQE objective addresses reduction mammaplasty directly.

testable_competencies.indications: Recognize the symptomatic indications for breast reduction (musculoskeletal pain, bra-strap grooving, intertrigo) as distinct from a diagnostic breast-mass workup.

do_not_test: Pedicle-technique selection and specific skin-resection pattern (specialist operative planning).

entries.title: Mastopexy (Breast Lift)

testable_competencies.awareness: General awareness that mastopexy addresses ptosis (position) rather than volume, distinguishing it conceptually from reduction/augmentation.

entries.zero_question_reason: Purely elective/cosmetic procedure with no MCC objective anchor and no generalist decision-making value beyond basic terminology; retained only as background differentiation from reduction/augmentation.

entries.title: Breast Augmentation

testable_competencies.complication_awareness: Recognize implant-related complications a generalist may encounter in follow-up (capsular contracture presentation, and awareness that breast implants carry a rare association with BIA-ALCL warranting referral for new peri-implant swelling/effusion).

do_not_test: Implant type/plane selection and augmentation operative technique (specialist procedural detail).

entries.title: Gynecomastia

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 10-1's key objective explicitly names gynecomastia: 'given a patient with a breast mass or gynecomastia, the candidate will diagnose the cause, severity, and urgency, and will initiate an appropriate management plan.'

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Differentiate physiologic (neonatal, pubertal, senescent) from pathologic gynecomastia and generate a cause-directed differential (drug-induced, hepatic, endocrine, testicular tumor) with appropriate workup.

do_not_test: Surgical technique selection for gynecomastia correction (liposuction vs. excision) -- specialist detail.

entries.title: Breast Reconstruction (Post-Mastectomy)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Post-mastectomy reconstruction is downstream of the breast-mass/cancer diagnostic pathway covered generally by objective 10-1, though reconstruction technique itself has no dedicated MCC objective.

testable_competencies.awareness: Recognize that immediate or delayed breast reconstruction (implant-based or autologous flap) is an option to discuss after mastectomy, as part of comprehensive post-cancer-treatment counselling.

do_not_test: Flap selection (latissimus dorsi, TRAM, DIEP), implant-vs-autologous decision-making, and nipple-reconstruction technique (specialist reconstructive detail).
entries.cross_discipline_note: Downstream of breast cancer management, which is primarily General/Thoracic Surgery and Gynecology/Oncology territory. PRIMARY_OWNER/CROSS_LINK deferred to global cross-chapter audit.

entries.title: Aesthetic (Cosmetic) Procedures Overview

testable_competencies.terminology: General terminology recognition for common elective cosmetic procedures (rhinoplasty, blepharoplasty, liposuction, etc.) for informed patient discussion/counselling.

entries.zero_question_reason: Purely elective cosmetic procedure catalogue with no MCC objective anchor and no generalist diagnostic/management decision-value; a graduating generalist is not expected to select or perform these procedures.

entries.title: Gender-Affirming Surgery

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 94-1 requires providing respectful, unbiased care and appropriate support/management measures for gender- and sexuality-related patient needs -- the generalist-relevant angle of this content (respectful counselling, awareness that gender-affirming surgical options exist and require multidisciplinary referral) is directly covered; the objective does not address specific operative techniques.

testable_competencies.counselling: Provide respectful, informed counselling to a transgender patient about the existence of gender-affirming surgical options and the referral pathway, without needing procedure-level technical knowledge.

do_not_test: Specific operative technique for chest/facial masculinization, vocal cord surgery, phalloplasty/metoidioplasty (explicitly redirected in-text to Urology, and specialist reconstructive detail regardless).
entries.cross_discipline_note: Explicit in-text redirect to Urology (Transition-Related Surgeries, U47) for genital gender-affirming procedures. PRIMARY_OWNER/CROSS_LINK vs. Urology deferred to global cross-chapter ownership audit.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 36-2 directly covers investigating congenital anomalies/dysmorphic features and identifying patients requiring early specialized referral -- craniofacial anomalies (cleft lip/palate, craniosynostosis) are a canonical example, though no dedicated cleft-lip/craniosynostosis MCC objective exists individually.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize common pediatric craniofacial anomalies (cleft lip/palate, craniosynostosis) on newborn/infant exam and identify the need for early multidisciplinary craniofacial-team referral.

entries.title: Congenital Hand Anomalies

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 36-2 covers congenital anomaly investigation/severity assessment and early-referral identification, applicable to congenital hand anomalies broadly, though the detailed ASSH classification itself has no dedicated MCC objective.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize major categories of congenital hand anomaly (syndactyly, polydactyly, radial club hand, constriction band syndrome) as findings warranting pediatric/hand-surgery referral, without requiring detailed ASSH sub-classification.

do_not_test: Full ASSH classification detail and syndrome-association lists (specialist-level classification detail).
